english.title: Assault a member of a National Crime Agency led international joint investigation team
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) assaulted **(..SPECIFY NAME..), a member of a National Crime Agency-led international joint investigation team who was carrying out functions as a member of the team
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 3(1) and (2) of Schedule 4 to the Crime and Courts Act 2013.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant assaulted **(..SPECIFY NAME..), a member of an National Crime Agency-led international joint investigation team who was carrying out functions as a member of the team.

other.penalty:
Summary: 51 weeks imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.

Note:
Until the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (alteration of penalties for summary offences) the reference to the period of 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to the period of 6 months.

Time limit on prosecutions:
Six months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
